title: How a Tsunami Crosses an Ocean

segments.say: Five hundred miles an hour. That is how fast a tsunami can race across the deep ocean, as fast as a jet plane.

anim.title: How it starts
items: The sea floor jerks up or down
The whole column of water above moves
Waves spread out in every direction

segments.say: It begins when an earthquake or a volcano makes the sea floor move suddenly. The whole column of water above it is pushed, and waves spread out.
Out in deep water, the waves are very long but very low. A ship may rise only a metre or two, so slowly that the crew hardly notices.
Near the coast the water gets shallow. The wave slows, its length shrinks, and its height grows, sometimes into a wall of water.
That is why a tsunami does little harm out at sea, and so much at the shore, where people live and work.

anim.title: India's watch
items: India joined the international warning system

segments.say: After the Indian Ocean tsunami of December two thousand four, India joined the international warning system. Its warnings now come from INCOIS in Hyderabad.

anim.below: in deep water; slow & high at the shore

segments.say: For GS One and disaster management: deep water means fast and low. Shallow water means slow and high.

sources: NOAA/NWS Tsunami.gov FAQ: in the deep ocean tsunamis can move over 500 mph, like a jet plane, and cross oceans in less than a day; wavelength 60–300 miles; deep-ocean waves rarely more than three feet high

NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 6 (Natural Hazards and Disasters): tsunamis caused by sudden sea-floor movement from earthquakes and volcanic eruptions; a ship rises only a metre or two and each rise and fall takes several minutes; in shallow water wavelength reduces and height increases; India joined the International Tsunami Warning System after the December 2004 tsunami
INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, Ministry of Earth Sciences) is in Hyderabad and runs India's tsunami early warning (Wikipedia summary of INCOIS)

quiz.q: How fast can a tsunami travel in the deep ocean?
options: It does not move until it reaches land
quiz.why: Over 500 mph (about 800 km/h) in deep water.

quiz.q: What happens to a tsunami as it enters shallow water?
options: It slows down and grows taller
quiz.why: Shallow water shortens the wave and raises its height.

quiz.q: Which institution issues India's tsunami warnings?
quiz.why: India's tsunami early warning comes from INCOIS in Hyderabad.
